title: F04 — Sync engine
tagline: one engine that moves every synced table between devices; projects, sessions and locations (F03) go first.

series.name: SiteLog: an iOS app and its API, built

intro: Sprint S2 · 45h · skeleton guide — full code is added when this feature starts.
Code in this guide is a teaching example. Check current source and follow F00 localization rules before applying it.

blocks.html:
• Goal: one engine that moves every synced table between devices; projects, sessions and locations (F03) go first.
  • Demo — offline: edits queue in an outbox; the Sync tab says how many are waiting; relaunch keeps them.
  • Demo — signed in: two devices on one account converge within one interval; deletes propagate; an exported session never reopens.
  • Spec: 08.2 Protocol, 08.3 Client engine, 03-backend §6
  • Starts from: F02 (ID token, HTTPClient) and F03 (first syncable tables).
  • Steps: How every feature runs. The engine is built against an in-memory server in step 3, so most of the logic is done before the backend exists.

sections.title: 3. Fake data — engine over in-memory data sources

blocks.html:
Overview

  • Goal: the real engine — pull, push, conflicts, deletes — written once, against an outbox and a server that live in memory.
  • Split into tasks when you start: queue · push · pull · conflicts · deletes.
ActionFileHolds
NewDataSources/Local/Sync/SyncLocalDataSource.swift + ImplOutbox (mutations in dependency order) and cursor; in memory
NewDataSources/Remote/Sync/SyncRemoteDataSource.swift + ImplIn-memory server: per-user rev counter, rows, LWW on clientUpdatedAt, tombstones
NewDataSources/Local/Persistence/SyncableLocalDataSource.swiftProtocol a table's data source adopts: table, apply(rows:)
NewRepositories/SyncRepositoryImpl.swiftActor: push → pull → pull again if serverRev moved; adopts superseded; logs every cycle
NewApp/DI/SyncTablesDI.swiftOrdered list of syncable data sources: projects → locations → sessions
  • Check: a test-only second engine on the same in-memory server sees the first one's project.

Steps

  1. Triggers: foreground, network restored, every syncInterval, outbox reaching pushBatchSize — never per write.
  2. sessions.state only moves forward; captures are insert-only.
  3. Every cycle logs {pulled, pushed, superseded, elapsedMs, cursor}.

blocks.html:
3. Fake data

  • LWW tie-break by id
  • Monotonic session state across all 16 pairs
  • 200 mutations = one request
  • Tombstones never resurrect
  • superseded adopts the server row

5. Local

  • Outbox survives relaunch; row and outbox row are saved together or not at all

6. Backend

  • In site-log-be: test/sync.test.ts (its tests)

7. Sync

  • Resync from 0 reproduces the store
  • Token expiry mid-sync loses nothing
  • Convergence test in CI
